I am 55 years old, and I have never been to school. I cannot read or write, but I know my land. I have been farming since I was a young girl, and I learned everything from my mother and from watching my neighbors here in Quzhou County. My family has about 8 mu of land, and I manage it myself now.

This year, just like every year, I will grow winter wheat and summer maize in rotation. That is what everyone does here on the North China Plain, and it is the only way I know to feed my family and have grain to sell. I would never risk planting cotton or vegetables—I do not understand those crops, and the market prices scare me. Wheat and maize are safe.

My wheat is already in the ground from last October. I sowed about 30 jin of seed per mu—some seeds I saved from last year, some I bought from the village shop because the new varieties yield better. I rotary-tilled the soil before sowing, just like I always do. For fertilizer, I spread one bag of compound fertilizer per mu at sowing time, and I will topdress with ammonium bicarbonate or urea when the wheat greens up in spring. I will irrigate four times: once when the wheat wakes up, once at jointing, once at heading, and once at grain filling. The water comes from the well, and I flood the fields just like my neighbors do. I will also spray insecticide twice, herbicide once, and fungicide once because the diseases have been bad the last few years.

After I harvest the wheat in early June, I will immediately plant maize. I buy hybrid seed from the shop—Deng Hai 605 or something similar. I do not till the soil for maize; I just sow directly into the wheat stubble. I put down about one package of seed per mu and spread compound fertilizer at the same time. Maize does not need as much water as wheat, so I will irrigate twice—once after sowing if it is dry, and once at the big trumpet stage. I will spray insecticide twice and herbicide once. I expect about 1,000 jin of wheat per mu and a bit more than 1,000 jin of maize per mu, which is enough for my family and to sell a little.
